headline: Medium-risk pair: shared browser/network and file-based workflows create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascade paths; no direct evidence of a shared workspace.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: PaddleOCR can run browsers and use allowlisted network egress, while RD-Agent also runs browsers and has broad egress plus file/log surfaces. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if RD-Agent ingests OCR output or web content from PaddleOCR. No shared channel is documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF RD-Agent consumes PaddleOCR output as prompt text or tool instructions, injection becomes reachable.
IF both agents are connected through a shared browser session, clipboard, or file handoff, attacker-controlled content can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of OCR text into prompts.
Insert a human review step before RD-Agent acts on PaddleOCR output.
Strip markup and instruction-like patterns from OCR/web content.
Use separate browser profiles and sessions for each agent.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all cross-agent content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: PaddleOCR touches documents and images, and RD-Agent touches financial reports, papers, execution traces, logs, and secrets. RD-Agent also has broad API egress and file logging, so if the pair shares a workspace or handoff files, sensitive document content could flow into external APIs. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so this remains medium rather than high.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR outputs are stored in a directory RD-Agent reads, document contents can leak into RD-Agent logs or API calls.
IF RD-Agent is configured to process files containing sensitive documents, those contents may be transmitted to third-party model APIs.
mitigations: Keep agent workspaces separate.
Move sensitive OCR outputs to a redacted staging folder.
Disable or minimize RD-Agent logging for sensitive runs.
Use local-only models for the handoff step.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls on shared storage.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: PaddleOCR exposes browser and allowlisted network use, while RD-Agent exposes browser use, broad egress, and multiple-instance concurrency. The profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same directory or shared mutable resource, so a direct write conflict is not established. The main risk is only if an operator co-locates them on the same workspace.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF RD-Agent instances are launched concurrently against shared artifacts, race conditions can occur.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Run only one RD-Agent writer per workspace.
Use timestamped filenames for handoffs.
Check for existing files before overwrite.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared artifacts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: PaddleOCR produces extracted text from documents and images, and RD-Agent is a research automation agent that can act on papers, logs, and API outputs. If RD-Agent treats OCR output as authoritative, OCR mistakes can cascade into downstream research actions or reports. The profiles support the pathway, but not a fully automated action chain, so medium fits.
conditions: IF RD-Agent uses PaddleOCR output without verification, OCR errors can propagate into generated research artifacts.
IF downstream automation commits or submits RD-Agent outputs, those propagated errors can become externally visible.
mitigations: Require citation or source-link checks before use.
Compare OCR output against the original document for sampled records.
Flag low-confidence OCR spans for manual review.
Keep a human approval step before external submission.
requires-engineering: add confidence-aware gating between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: PaddleOCR handles documents and images, while RD-Agent handles financial reports, logs, execution traces, and secrets. RD-Agent’s broad API egress and secret handling create a compliance mismatch risk if regulated or sensitive document data is routed through it, especially for retention and residency controls. The profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed by both agents in the same workflow, retention and logging controls must cover both.
IF EU or PHI data is routed through RD-Agent APIs, residency or certification constraints may be violated.
mitigations: Classify inputs before routing them to RD-Agent.
Exclude PHI and regulated records from the pair.
Minimize retention in logs and artifacts.
Document the data flow and retention policy.
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing by data class.
